dgs2.label: 2-Year Treasury
dgs2.note: What the US government pays to borrow for two years. Moves on what the market expects the Fed to do next.

dgs10.label: 10-Year Treasury
dgs10.note: The long rate most other borrowing costs — mortgages included — are priced off.

dgs30.label: 30-Year Treasury
dgs30.note: The longest point on the curve. Reflects what the market thinks inflation and growth look like decades out.

cpi.label: US CPI Inflation
cpi.note: Consumer price index for all urban consumers, all items, against the same month a year earlier.

unrate.label: US Unemployment Rate
unrate.note: Share of the US labour force without a job and looking for one. Seasonally adjusted.

cacpi.label: Canada CPI Inflation
cacpi.note: Canadian all-items consumer price index against the same month a year earlier.

caunrate.label: Canada Unemployment Rate
caunrate.note: Share of the Canadian labour force without a job and looking for one. Seasonally adjusted.

sp500pe.label: S&P 500 P/E
sp500pe.note: What a dollar of the index’s trailing annual earnings costs. History runs to 1871, which is long enough to see that the long-run average sits in the mid-teens and that every number above it has had an explanation at the time.
